The bounded render classification (PassThroughReason/FailureReason/SourceFailureReason) on the artwork log line.

The bounded classification is emitted when present; ADR-020 clause 4 is amended (subject added, directory/full-path exclusion added) and the log path is security-reviewed.

deliverables: A bytes<->unit conversion helper with a fixed per-field MB/KB mapping, step, and precision, and unit-labelled validation ranges.
The authoritative, code-evidenced restart-required set (task 16.2 as single owner), including mixed settings classified restart-required.
Restart-required note text on the settings page.
The modal reminder (subject to the jellyfin-expert spike) with note text as the fail-open behavior.
ADR-028 and the canonical documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Byte limits are displayed in a fixed per-field binary unit with validation ranges in the same unit and precision; min/default/max round-trip exactly, including the 64 KiB minima; a range that spans 1 MiB stays in the field's unit; the persisted XML and internal values stay bytes.
The restart-required set is code-owned, evidenced, and testable, with mixed settings classified restart-required.
Every restart-required setting in the settings page carries note text (a mixed setting's note text also states that some paths apply immediately).
The modal fires on change when the modal API is available and falls back to the note text otherwise.

phases.name: Reconciliation coverage and version-aware coalescing
phases.objective: Guarantee successive-run coverage of a scope larger than QueueCapacity and stop a post-save re-render from being dropped by version-blind coalescing.
deliverables: The accepted F4 mechanism (ADR-022, Accepted (v1.2): a persisted (SortName, itemId) cursor, a bounded enqueue-outcome vocabulary, and a resume-capable IMediaLibraryEnumerator) with a bounded Cache-authority state record and scope-reset rule.
F4 successive-run coverage tests, including the coalesce/in-flight/overflow and library-mutation cases.
The accepted F6 mechanism (ADR-023, Accepted (v1.2): a ConfigurationStale discard classification with a bounded re-enqueue after the in-flight slot is released).
F6 coalescing coverage tests, including the pre-slot-release failure case.
ADR-022/ADR-023 and the architecture documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Successive scheduled/post-scan runs cover a scope larger than QueueCapacity (round-robin) with one run still bounded; a coalesced or in-flight item does not stall the run and the run stops at the first overflow.
The cursor is a bounded, secret-free Cache-authority (SortName, itemId) record that resets on scope change and on a missing/torn/out-of-range record and is stable under library mutation.
Event, webhook, per-item, and post-save triggers are unchanged and do not read or write the cursor.

A ConfigurationStale discard re-enqueues one current-version work item after the in-flight slot is released, bounded per (item, connection, surface, version), while a non-version discard does not re-enqueue and the version-blind key and single-flight are unchanged.

tasks.name: F4 mechanism confirmation and persisted-cursor implementation
tasks.acceptance_criteria: DG-19/ADR-022 is accepted (Accepted (v1.2)) and the implementation follows it: the scheduled/post-scan reconciliation advances a bounded, versioned, secret-free Cache-authority cursor over the deterministic `(SortName, itemId)` total order and wraps at the end; the enqueue boundary returns the Accepted/Coalesced/InFlight/Overflow/Stopped vocabulary; a coalesced or in-flight item is covered without stalling and the run stops at the first overflow, advancing the cursor only over the covered prefix; the cursor resets on a scope change and on a missing/torn/out-of-range record; post-save does not read or write the cursor; one run remains bounded.

tasks.name: F4 successive-run coverage tests
tasks.traceability: F4; ADR-022 clause 5; verification requirements section 9
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Tests prove that successive runs over a scope larger than QueueCapacity cover the whole scope over time, that the cursor wraps, that a scope change resets it, and that event/webhook/per-item/post-save triggers do not read or write it; tests cover the coalesce, in-flight, overflow-stop, and library-mutation (stable seek key) cases.

tasks.name: F6 mechanism confirmation and stale-basis re-enqueue implementation
tasks.acceptance_criteria: DG-20/ADR-023 is accepted (Accepted (v1.2)) and the implementation follows it: a ConfigurationStale discard re-enqueues exactly one fresh work item at the current configuration version after the in-flight slot is released, bounded to one per (item, connection, surface, version) by the carried current version; a same-version discard, a stopped or full queue, and a discard with any other classification (ItemMissing/Ineligible/ConnectionChanged/IdentityUnavailable) do not re-enqueue; an item that became ineligible/absent is re-enqueued once and then discarded for its real reason; WorkItemKey stays version-blind and single-flight is preserved.

tasks.name: F6 coalescing coverage tests
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Tests reproduce the post-save coalescing case (new-version hint coalesced while the item is pending or in flight) and prove the item re-renders at the current version without a loop or duplicate concurrent work; a coverage test fails if the re-enqueue is issued before the in-flight slot is released, and a test proves a non-version discard does not re-enqueue.

risks: G9: the log subject exposes a directory path or a sensitive file name. Mitigated by ADR-026's bounded file-name-only subject with item-id fallback, no directory, redaction tests at every verbosity, and a fresh logging security review (15.1-15.4).

F3: the diagnostics endpoint leaks a secret or an unbounded payload. Mitigated by ADR-025's elevation-gated read-only endpoint, fixed bounded shape, no per-item listing, and a dedicated security review (17.2, 17.4).

F4: the coverage cursor corrupts or stalls reconciliation. Mitigated by a bounded Cache-authority (SortName, itemId) cursor with a scope reset and a start fallback, the bounded enqueue-outcome vocabulary that does not stall on coalesce/in-flight and stops at the first overflow, plus coverage tests (19.1, 19.2).

F6: the re-enqueue loops, is coalesced away, or duplicates work. Mitigated by the ConfigurationStale discard classification, the re-enqueue after the in-flight slot is released, the current-version bound, the unchanged version-blind key, and preserved single-flight, plus coalescing coverage tests (19.3, 19.4).

F7: the restore removes correct artwork on a transient failure. Mitigated by restoring/removing only for an owned empty resolved selection (NoDisplayableValue) through ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync and the guarded protocol, preserving the current artwork for every other reason including NoFittingBadge (20.1, 20.2).

G7: the Extra Large change unexpectedly alters existing output. Mitigated by the requirement that existing goldens stay byte-identical and the no-advance decision, with a changed existing golden reopening the decision (18.1, 18.2).
G6/G8: the restart-required classification is wrong. Mitigated by making it code-owned and code-evidenced and by testing the per-operation set against a replaced snapshot (16.2).

findings.closure: ADR-022 clause 1 defines the bounded enqueue-outcome vocabulary (Accepted / Coalesced / InFlight / Overflow / Stopped) on IWorkHintSink's result-returning call; clause 2 defines the exact cursor-advance rule (covered on Accepted/Coalesced/InFlight and on correctly-no-hint items; stop at the first Overflow/Stopped; continue past coalesce). Plan F4 acceptance and PLANS.md Phase 19 acceptance updated.

ADR-022 clause 3 defines a stable (SortName, itemId) seek key over a total order with an item-id tie-break and a resume-capable IMediaLibraryEnumerator; add/remove does not reset the cursor, and coverage is guaranteed for a stable library and best-effort under concurrent mutation. Plan F4 acceptance and task 19.1/19.2 updated.

ADR-023 clause 3 requires the re-enqueue after CompleteProcessing releases the in-flight slot, dropping when stopped/full; plan F6 acceptance and task 19.4 require a coverage test that fails if the re-enqueue is issued before the slot is released.

ADR-023 clause 1 defines a bounded DiscardReason (ConfigurationStale / ItemMissing / Ineligible / ConnectionChanged / IdentityUnavailable); clause 2 states only ConfigurationStale re-enqueues; plan F6 and task 19.3/19.4 require a test that a non-version discard does not re-enqueue.

ADR-024 clause 1 narrows NoDisplayableValue to an empty resolved selection and adds a distinct NoFittingBadge pass-through reason for a non-empty layout-empty render; plan F7 and task 20.1/20.2 require a coverage test that a non-empty selection which cannot fit performs no mutation.

ADR-028 clause 1 defines the unit selection per field (MB, KB for WebhookMaxPayloadBytes), a per-field step (64 KiB for the three 64-KiB-min fields; 1 MiB/1 KiB otherwise), the display precision, the exact conversion algorithm (scaled-decimal parse, round to nearest byte, step-validation), and the range label when the range spans 1 MiB. Plan G6 acceptance and task 16.1 updated.
ADR-022 clause 4 fixes the cursor StateAuthority to Cache (invalid/torn -> discarded/miss -> start), the fixed kind reconciliation-cursor and a fixed record id, and the bounded scope-identity tuple.

ADR-022 clause 6 excludes PostSave from the cursor and gives the reason (bounded user-triggered prefix re-cover); plan F4 decision/acceptance and PLANS.md add post-save to the unaffected-trigger list.

ADR-023 clause 4 defines the bound as implicit in the current version carried by the re-enqueued item (no separate version set); clause 5 restates that an ineligible/absent item is re-enqueued once then discarded for its real reason, consistent with the version check preceding item resolve/eligibility.

ADR-024 clause 2 names the pass-through site (ArtworkGenerationCoordinator) and the internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync entry point under ArtworkLifecycleFence.Normal and the existing subject gate/recovery; clause 3 confirms Normal-fence restoration is intended and crash-recoverable via ArtworkRecoveryDecisions.

ADR-026 Status/Context/clause 4 rewritten: ADR-020 clause 4 has no path exclusion; the amendment adds the bounded log subject to the allowed set and adds an explicit directory/full-path exclusion, dropping the 'still never logged' overclaim.

ADR-026 clause 3 enumerates every item-id-emitting site and its available subject, including MetadataReconciliationProcessor.Discard as a mixed site, and requires the helper to fall back to the item id when no path exists; plan G9 acceptance and task 15.2 updated.

ADR-028 clause 2 classifies a mixed setting as restart-required if ANY consumer captures, with note text stating some paths apply immediately, and requires task 16.2 to record per-consumer evidence; plan G8 and task 16.2/16.3 updated.

ADR-028 Context marks the examples illustrative; clause 2 makes task 16.2 the single owner of the complete evidenced set, naming ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes and the per-operation ProviderResponseLimitBytes, WebhookMaxPayloadBytes, and InventoryCacheMaxBytes plus the mixed limits. Per-phase docs are owned by task 16.6/21.2.
